_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The test seeds two conversations: A at /c/catchup-a, whose reply reads "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.", and B at /c/catchup-b, whose reply reads "Well, hi there!". A conversation "shows" a text when document.querySelector(".messages-container")?.textContent includes it (wait for that with an eval expecting true, allowing 15s; do not look elsewhere on the page, as the conversation list previews messages too). To "select" a conversation with slug X: click the button[aria-label="Open conversations"]; wait for ".drawer.open" to be visible (allow 5s); wait for the ".drawer.open .conversation-title" whose text is exactly X to be visible (allow 15s) and click it; then wait for ".drawer.open" to be hidden (allow 10s). Perform the steps in order. A reload preserves the cache: no spinner, and no backfill after the reload. Call "track" starts counting the browser's GETs of A's full-load endpoint (/api/conversation/<A's id>, any query) and call "A loads" returns how many there have been since, as a number.
1. Navigate to /c/catchup-a; wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s); A shows "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.".
2. Reload the page; wait for the message input to be visible (allow 30s); A shows "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant." (the IndexedDB cache rehydrates it).
3. There must be exactly 0 ".spinner" elements.
4. Call "track".
5. Select catchup-b; it shows "Well, hi there!".
6. Select catchup-a; it shows "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.".
7. Call "A loads": it must return exactly "0": the B → A round trip after the reload must be served from the cache.
